descriptionModule.briefSummary:
The ASPIRE-GCA Pilot trial will assess the feasibility of a future randomized controlled trial (RCT) evaluating the efficacy of low-dose ASA in preventing ischemic complications in patients with Giant Cell Arteritis (GCA).

ASPIRE-GCA Pilot builds on extensive preparatory work and the findings from this study will inform key feasibility outcomes, including recruitment rate, study-drug delivery and treatment initiation, medication adherence, participant retention, and completeness of follow-up data.
descriptionModule.detailedDescription:
ASPIRE-GCA Pilot is a national, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, decentralized trial conducted in centers of the Canadian Vasculitis Research Network (CanVasc), designed to evaluate the feasibility of conducting the full international RCT.

To examine this objective, 120 eligible patients with newly diagnosed GCA will be randomized at a 1:1 ratio to receive low-dose ASA (80 mg/day) or placebo for 52 weeks, in addition to standard-of-care therapy for GCA. Participants will then be followed for 13 months.

maskingInfo.maskingDescription: Participants, treating clinicians, investigators, outcome adjudicators, and data analysts will remain blinded through completion of the analyses.

armGroups.label: Acetyl Salicylic Acid (ASA)
armGroups.description: Participants will receive low-dose ASA (80 mg orally once daily) for 52 weeks, in addition to standard-of-care therapy for GCA.

armGroups.label: Control Arm
armGroups.description: Participants will receive a matching low-dose ASA placebo (orally once daily) for 52 weeks, in addition to standard-of-care therapy for GCA.

interventions.name: Acetyl Salicylic Acid (ASA)
interventions.description: Participants will receive blinded low-dose ASA (80 mg orally once daily) for 52 weeks.

interventions.name: Placebo
interventions.description: Participants will receive blinded low-dose ASA placebo (orally once daily) for 52 weeks.

primaryOutcomes.measure: Recruitment rate defined as the number of participants randomized per center-month.
primaryOutcomes.description: Number of participants randomized per center-month, counting each center from the date it is activated and able to enroll participants until completion of recruitment.
primaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Through study completion, an average of 18 months

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Study treatment initiation, assessed as the proportion of randomized participants who initiate study treatment.
Time to study treatment initiation, assessed as the number of days from randomization to first study treatment administration among randomized participants who initiate treatment.
Treatment adherence, assessed using the proportion of days covered.
secondaryOutcomes.description: The proportion of days covered is calculated as the number of days covered by the dispensed study medication divided by the total number of days in the treatment period, multiplied by 100.

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Participant retention, defined as the proportion of randomized participants completing the 12-month follow-up visit.
Completeness of follow-up data, assessed as the proportion of randomized participants completing the 12-month visit for whom all clinical outcome data required for the definitive trial are available.
Study-drug delivery performance, assessed as the proportion of participants experiencing ≥1 delivery-related delay resulting in delayed treatment initiation or treatment interruption.
Barriers for recruitment, assessed by the frequency of reasons for ineligibility.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Through study completion, an average of 18 months

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Barriers for adherence, assessed by the frequency of reasons for treatment discontinuation.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Through study completion, an average of 18 months

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Barriers for retention, assessed by the frequency of reasons for withdrawal from the trial.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Through study completion, an average of 18 months

otherOutcomes.measure: Time to first ischemic event (in days)
otherOutcomes.description: The efficacy composite outcome of the full trial will be the time to first ischemic event, defined as the first occurence of ischemic death, new ischemic vision loss, ischemic stroke, transient ischemic attack, myocardial infarction, unstable angina requiring hospitalization, or acute limb ischemia requiring intervention.

otherOutcomes.measure: Time to first major bleeding event (in days)
otherOutcomes.description: Major bleeding is defined according to the Bleeding Academic Research Consortium criteria.
